image_description: Two bison standing on a paved road next to a wooden fence post. The foreground bison is dark brown with a prominent shoulder hump and shaggy fur, facing right. The background bison is lighter reddish-brown, partially obscured by the fence post, facing left. A sign reading 'Canyon Overlook' is visible in the background among trees.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both bison display large, broad heads. The foreground bison clearly shows short, curved black horns consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground bison has a distinct, shaggy beard hanging from its chin and throat area.
The eye of the foreground bison is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the checkpoint.
Ears are not prominently sticking out; they appear small and are largely blended into the thick fur of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both animals exhibit the characteristic massive build and high withers typical of bison.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground bison has a very pronounced shoulder hump covered in thick, shaggy dark brown fur. The texture looks dense and realistic.
There is a visible transition from the shaggy front to smoother, shorter hair on the rear flanks of both bison.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horns are proportionally small relative to the massive head and body size.

While the legs are sturdy, the feet/hooves of the foreground bison are somewhat blurry and indistinct against the pavement. The specific 'cloven' detail is not sharply resolved, appearing more as a solid dark mass due to resolution or generation softness.
The tails of both bison are either occluded by their own bodies or the angle makes them invisible. Cannot verify.

artifact_observations.location: Foreground bison's front left hoof/leg bottom
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection between the leg and the ground is slightly soft/melted. The hoof structure lacks sharp definition, blending slightly into the shadow/pavement.

The rear legs of the background bison appear to merge or fade into the background scenery/fence line unnaturally. The anatomy of the hind legs is vague and lacks clear separation from the environment.
The wooden rail attached to the post seems to float or attach at an awkward angle relative to the post's geometry, suggesting slight spatial inconsistency.
